entries.content: (a-0) (The title of this book, 'Ezra'), Meaning, 'Help.'
Sheshbazzar (a-21) This appears to be the Chaldean name of Zerubbabel, which may mean, 'Born in Babylon.'
chargers (b-9) chargers (b-14) Large shallow basons or dishes, either for the blood of sprinkling or fine flour offerings. see Num. 7.13; 1Kings 7.40. The word only occurs in this passage.
basons (c-2) basons (c-6) See 1Chron. 28.17.
children (d-5) Lit. 'sons.' province, (e-8) i.e. of Judah. see ch. 5.8; Neh. 1.3.
Zerubbabel, (f-4) Sheshbazzar; ch. 1.8; see 1Chron. 3.19.
Gibbar, (g-4) Neh. 7.25. Gibeon.
Nethinim. (a-2) Subordinate temple servants. see ch. 8.20; 1Chron. 9.2, and Num. 8.19.
Meunim, (b-8) Or 'the Maonites.' see 2Chron. 20.1. Nephusim, (c-12) Or 'the Nephusites,' from Naphish. 1Chron. 1.31.
Tirshatha (a-3) Title of governor of Jerusalem under Persian kings. Thummim. (b-27) See Neh. 7.65.
darics (c-14) * A Persian gold coin weighing about 130 grains. See 1Chron. 29.7. The pound is the Hebrew maneh, about 50 shekels in money. see Neh. 7.71; Ezek. 45.12.
required; (d-28) Lit. 'the thing of a day.'
superintend (e-67) Or 'set forward.'
Judah, (a-17) Or rather, 'Hodavia.' see ch. 2.40.
alternately (b-4) See Note, Ps. 119.172.
Ahasuerus, (c-6) Probably Cambyses, son of Cyrus.
Artaxerxes, (d-6) Smerdis. Aramaic. (e-35) From here to ch. 6.18 the original is written in Aramaic.

river, (a-32) Strictly, 'beyond the river,' a technical name for the provinces on the west of the Euphrates. In English the expression has to be varied, in accordance with the position of the persons in question. cities (f-19) Lit. 'city.'
kings. (b-37) Others, 'and thou wilt endamage the kings' revenue.'

God (c-9) Aramaic, Elah (Heb. Eloah. see Gen. 1.1). The parts of the book written in Aramaic are chs. 4.8 to 6.18, and ch. 7.12 to 26; they have always Elah. El does not occur in Ezra. Darius (d-25) Darius Hystaspes, as ch. 4.5.
Achmetha (a-6) Ecbatana, capital of Great Media. fortress (b-9) Or 'capital.'
decree (a-12) Elsewhere, 'gave orders.'
Artaxerxes, (a-9) Most probably Artaxerxes Longimanus, son of Xerxes, Esther 1.1.
on, (b-18) Others, 'he began the going up.'
ordinances. (c-26) Lit. 'statute and ordinance.'
Israel. (d-34) The Aramaic is resumed as far as ver. 26.
accomplished (e-10) Others translate, 'a scribe of ... of heavens. perfect [peace].'
by (f-5) Lit. 'from before.'
offer (a-19) Lit. 'present,' as ch. 6.10,17.
measures (b-11) Koreen, same as Hebrew cor. see Note, 2Chron. 27.5.
banishment, (c-29) Lit. 'uprooting.'
namely, (a-31) Or 'and.'
humble (b-14) Or 'afflict.' right (c-24) Or 'plain.'
basons (a-3) See ch. 1.10, and 1Chron. 28.17. shining (b-14) Lit. 'good shining.'
governors (c-14) Or 'pachas.' so Neh. 2.7, &c.
rulers (d-33) Segan, a Persian word.
nail (a-27) Or 'tent-pin.' see Isa. 22.23.
wall (b-50) Or 'enclosing fence.' see Ezek. 13.5.
trespass, (c-17) Or rather 'guilt.' less (d-26) Or 'spared us more.'
lord, (e-30) The Hebrew text shows Adonai, 'the Lord.'
confiscated, (a-25) Lit. 'devoted by curse.'
against (b-15) Others 'stood over.'
Jaasai, (a-4) Or 'Jaasu.'
Jaddai, (b-10) Or 'Iddo.'
